tier_reason: Upgraded from C: the performance page source (gh-pages performance.md) names the CPU (Intel Core i7-11800H), compiler and flags (Clang 11.1.0, clang++ -Wall -O2 -march=native), Spectra v1.0.0, ARPACK-NG 3.7.0 and single-threaded OpenBLAS 0.3.15, and its bar charts are produced by the public benchmark program (benchmark/main.cpp, Makefile, F77 wrapper) run against ARPACK.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Performance page bar charts (median elapsed ms over 10 replicates, 10 random dense matrices per size, 10 eigenvalues; values read approximately from the plot images, ratios derived from page data): symmetric solver n=100 Spectra about 0.36-0.50 ms vs ARPACK about 0.53-0.68 ms (about 1.3x-1.5x), n=1000 about 20.5-25.7 ms vs 23.8-29.8 ms (about 1.15x-1.2x); general solver n=100 about 1.3-6.0 ms vs 1.8-9.7 ms (about 1.35x-1.6x), n=1000 about 184-317 ms vs 200-360 ms (about 1.0x-1.25x). Page text: the symmetric solver is uniformly faster than ARPACK in all tested cases and the general solver is almost identical to ARPACK.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Performance page: Clang 11.1.0, clang++ -Wall -O2 -march=native; OpenBLAS 0.3.15 single-threaded; ARPACK-NG 3.7.0 (its build flags not stated). Note the repo's benchmark/Makefile defaults to g++ -Wall -O2 and gfortran -O3 for the ARPACK wrapper.
corrections.hardware: Intel Core i7-11800H 2.30GHz x 16, 32GB RAM, Solus 4.2 64-bit
corrections.workload: benchmark/main.cpp: 10 random dense matrices (Eigen MatrixXd::Random; symmetric case A^T + A) of size n=100 (k=10, ncv=20) and n=1000 (k=10, ncv=30), 10 replicates each; Spectra SymEigsSolver/GenEigsSolver with DenseSymMatProd/DenseGenMatProd versus ARPACK's saupd/naupd reverse-communication routines called through the benchmark's F77.cpp and Fortran wrapper; median elapsed time.
corrections.caveats: Numbers exist only as bar-chart images on the performance page (spectralib.org/performance.html, served from the gh-pages branch); values here are approximate plot readings. Margins are modest (about 1.0x-1.6x) and were measured with Spectra v1.0.0 (2021). The test matrices are small random dense matrices, so the result says little about large sparse problems where the matrix-vector product dominates. The repo Makefile (g++ -O2) differs from the page's stated clang++ -O2 -march=native, and ARPACK-NG's own build flags are not given. Results depend on the BLAS/LAPACK ARPACK links against. ARPACK is not in the SuiteSparse/Eigen/PETSc baseline list (PETSc users reach it through SLEPc).

notes: spectralib.org is egress-blocked, but the page source is on the repo's gh-pages branch (performance.md plus img/benchmark-sym.png and img/benchmark-gen.png), which I opened and viewed; it confirms the excerpt's environment details. The charts show Spectra faster on every case including the general solver, which the page text calls almost identical (matrix 9 at n=1000 is about equal).
